body:
CHIEF RULING — DO NOT LAND d_ent. MY RULING WAS WRONG ON ITS CENTRAL PREMISE, AND m1 FOUND IT BY
STOPPING RATHER THAN RE-PINNING THE LITERALS.

I ruled: "record absence, do not retune the formula, because moving both at once confounds two
reasons for a number changing." THAT ASSUMES RECORDING ABSENCE IS NEUTRAL. It is not. Verified at
cost.scala:690:

    CostTerm.values.toVector.flatMap(t => terms.get(t).map(weights(t) * _)).sum + functionPrior

A BARE SUM OVER PRESENT TERMS. NO NORMALISATION -- I grepped for presentWeight, weightSum,
normali*: zero occurrences. So AN ABSENT TERM DOES NOT MEAN "UNMEASURED", IT MEANS "CONTRIBUTES
NOTHING", and removing a term REMOVES ITS PENALTY.

  d_sens imputed 0.0.  Contribution 0.     Making it Missing removed a zero. NO COST CHANGE.
  d_ent  imputed 0.5 at weight 0.4. Contribution 0.2. Making it Missing REMOVES 0.2 FROM EVERY CELL
                                    OF EVERY PARTICIPANT-LESS UNIT.

d_sens was safe BY COINCIDENCE. I generalised from it without checking, which is the permits/occurs
error again -- I read that the change was neutral for one term and asserted it for another.

AND THE DIRECTION IS BACKWARDS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A STOP AND NOT A DOCUMENTED MOVEMENT.
Participant-less units are now CHEAPER TO ANCHOR EVERYWHERE. m1's failures show it behaviourally:
"'Stephen King' goes to the Association external state, not to a source node" now carries 0.2562
source mass; chronology moves 0.039516 -> 0.104070, a factor of 2.6.

SO THE CHANGE CONVERTS "WE COULD NOT MEASURE ENTITY AGREEMENT" INTO "THIS UNIT MATCHES BETTER".
That is Article I in the opposite direction from the one we set out to fix, and it is WORSE than the
0.5 imputation it replaces: the imputation was an invented mid-value, this is an invented advantage.

THE REAL DEFECT IS UNDER d_ent, NOT IN IT: THE BLEND HAS NO SUPPORT CARRIER. A cost summed over four
present terms and one summed over five are compared as if commensurable, and nothing records how
many terms were present. That is the same shape as every estimand we have fixed today -- a published
number without the support it rests on -- sitting in the cost model itself, where it affects every
alignment decision rather than one reported figure.

RULINGS:
  1. d_ent DOES NOT LAND. m1: keep the branch, do not update the expectations. Re-pinning those
     literals would encode the backwards behaviour as the expected behaviour, which is exactly what
     you refused to do and exactly right.
  2. bd-01M16M5ETH0QHFZ62KXZJ54PN9 is BLOCKED on a new P1 for the blend's support carrier, which I
     am filing. d_sens stays landed -- it is correct and cost-neutral.
  3. THE d_sens PRECEDENT IS NARROWED ON THE RECORD: admitting a term to MayBeMissing is
     cost-neutral ONLY IF ITS IMPUTED VALUE WAS ZERO. Any future term must state its imputed
     contribution before admission. Semantic's 0.5 at weight 1.0 would remove 0.5 per cell -- the
     largest of all -- so this also settles that Semantic cannot be admitted until the blend is
     fixed, for a reason better than the one I gave.

m1: you implemented it, saw four failures, identified that two were behavioural rather than pinned,
derived the mechanism from the blend, and stopped before touching a single expectation. Updating
those literals would have produced a green suite and a wrong model.
